extracted.intended_audience: agency rulewriters, DOJ staff, regulatory policy analysts, legal researchers, and public stakeholders who prepare or use Federal Register regulatory agenda entries
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and publishing a Department of Justice entry in the Federal Register Regulatory Agenda, including required metadata, abstracts, timetable entries, and compliance with the Regulatory Flexibility Act (section 610) and Federal Register drafting conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official legal status and reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype XML rendition and is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register; it does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO’s govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar (govinfo.gov) for the official electronic format and verify results against an official edition when relying on material for legal research. Until ACFR grants official status, the XML rendition does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document headings required/typical content
rubrics_metrics.description: Document Headings vary by document type but may contain the agency, the CFR title and part numbers, the agency docket number/internal file number, the RIN which identifies regulatory actions, and other standard headings such as AGENCY:, ACTION:, SUMMARY:, FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:, SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Document Drafting Handbook for more details. The table of contents used on the site is a navigational tool processed from the headings; repetition of headings to form internal navigation links has no substantive legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 610 review periodicity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 610 of the Regulatory Flexibility Act requires agencies once every 10 years to review rules that have a significant economic impact upon a substantial number of small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must plan and publish Notices of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRMs) as necessary to conduct these periodic reviews (example: DOJ planning NPRMs to review ADA title II and title III regulations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of printed Regulatory Flexibility Agenda entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Because publication in the Federal Register is mandated for the regulatory flexibility agendas required by the Regulatory Flexibility Act, the Department's printed agenda entries include only: rules that are in the Agency's regulatory flexibility agenda (likely to have significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities) and any rules that the Agency has identified for periodic review under section 610.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printing of these entries is limited to fields that contain information required by the Regulatory Flexibility Act's Agenda requirements. Additional information on these entries is available in the Unified Agenda published online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable and metadata fields for agenda entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry includes a Timetable section with Action, Date, and FR Cite, and must indicate whether a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis is required, along with RIN and Agency Contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries commonly show Action (e.g., NPRM), Date (or 'To Be Determined'), FR Cite (when applicable), Regulatory Flexibility Analysis Required: Yes/No, Agency Contact name/office/address/phone, and RIN. Provide these fields consistently to meet Agenda requirements and to allow public tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency contact information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must list a point of contact for further information, including name, title, office, mailing address, and telephone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Robert Hinchman, Senior Counsel, Office of Legal Policy, Department of Justice, Room 4252, 950 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20530, (202) 514-8059.' Include current and accurate contact details to facilitate inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document identification and citation metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda documents include document citation (e.g., '90 FR 45532'), document number (e.g., '2025-18331'), document type (Notice), pages, and publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also include CFR chapter/parts affected (if any), sequence/identifier numbers for items in the Agenda, and RINs so users can cross-reference docket and Unified Agenda entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection and verification practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Inspection files (PDFs) show FR Docs as they appeared on Public Inspection and may indicate how many times they were viewed while on Public Inspection. If using public inspection listings for legal research, verify contents against a final, official edition of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only official editions of the Federal Register provide legal notice of publication to the public and judicial notice to the courts under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of machine-readable and alternate formats
rubrics_metrics.description: This document is also available in formats such as JSON (normalized attributes and metadata), XML (original full text XML), and MODS (GPO metadata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More information and documentation on these formats are available on developer tools pages; include links to alternate formats to assist researchers and developers who consume agenda data programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory action tracking and completion metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed Actions sections list the sequence number, title, legal authority, abstract, and a chronology of actions (e.g., NPRM date and FR cite, Final Rule date and FR cite, Final Action Effective date) along with a 'Completed: Reason' field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific FR citations and dates for each milestone (NPRM, Final Rule, Effective Date) and note whether a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis was required to enable tracking of rulemaking progress and status.
